source.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Wide Receiver Sleepers to Draft and Busts to Avoid
source.author: Zach Buckley
source.summary: Two receiver sleepers and two price-sensitive avoids.

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Stribling's explosiveness, second-round investment, and fit in San Francisco's yards-after-catch offense create an immediate path to routes.
takeaways.rationale: Stribling's explosiveness, second-round investment, and fit in San Francisco's yards-after-catch offense create an immediate path to routes.
risks: The veteran receiver room can reduce his role if healthy.

takeaways.label: avoid
takeaways.summary: Olave's third-round price carries more uncertainty than desired because of rookie target competition, quarterback volatility, and injury history.
takeaways.rationale: Olave's third-round price carries more uncertainty than desired because of rookie target competition, quarterback volatility, and injury history.
risks: His 2025 volume and production already proved a WR1 ceiling.

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: A full offseason in Seattle should create more designed touches for Shaheed's explosive skill set in an offense that may need more passing volume.
takeaways.rationale: A full offseason in Seattle should create more designed touches for Shaheed's explosive skill set in an offense that may need more passing volume.
risks: Seattle failed to integrate him after the trade and the role remains speculative.

takeaways.label: avoid
takeaways.summary: Wilson's talent remains clear, but uncertain quarterback improvement and new first-round target competition make his third- or fourth-round ceiling questionable.
takeaways.rationale: Wilson's talent remains clear, but uncertain quarterback improvement and new first-round target competition make his third- or fourth-round ceiling questionable.
risks: His historical target dominance can survive a difficult environment.
